source: Bell et al. (2021), MNRAS 504, 3316, 'A comprehensive reanalysis of Spitzer's 4.5 um phase curves, and the phase variations of the ultra-hot Jupiters MASCARA-1b and KELT-16b' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stab1027; arXiv:2010.00687). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of CoRoT-2b, program 11073, first published by Dang et al. (2018) and reanalysed here. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of preferred SPCA model parameters (tab:preferred), row CoRoT-2b, detector model Poly4. The preferred fit is first order (the caption of its figure names the mode Poly4_v1), so the printed semi-amplitude and offset are the whole phase variation (section 4.1: semi-amplitude sqrt(C1^2 + D1^2), offset east -arctan2(D1, C1)). CoRoT-2 is one of the three systems the paper corrects for a nearby star's light (section 4.1, Dilution Correction; tab:dilution gives C_corr = 1.2046 for CoRoT-2, applied to the radius ratio as sqrt(C_corr) and to the dayside flux as C_corr); tab:preferred does not say in its caption that its cells carry the correction.

model.equation: F_p = F_day [1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi], psi counted from mid-eclipse (section 4.1), printed as its semi-amplitude and the offset east of its maximum.
